messages:
incbot: PAGER: [SEV2] Elevated 5xxs and tail latency observed in ap-southeast1 inference tier. 5xx ~15% over last 5m, p95 latency +220ms. Auto failover hasn't kicked. Impact: hosted API users in APAC. Please acknowledge.

amanda: oncall here, ack. starting triage — pulling logs and route state.

leo: I'm seeing provider-a pod restarts and an OOM in the runtime logs. suspect bad batch sizing spike. attaching recent logs.

leo: ```
runtime: oom at gpu0
stack: kv_cache_alloc -> batch_assemble -> forward
metrics: batch_size_p50=48 -> p95=240
``` 

nirav: if runtime OOMs, we should soften batching + reduce concurrency first then consider provider reroute. proposing: scale provider-a down to 50% traffic, soft-quota ap-southeast1 to 60%, and set batching max to 64.

amanda: agree. leo, can you apply the batching cap? I'll coordinate traffic.

leo: applying batching cap now.

leo: ```
# apply batching cap
redwoodctl runtime update --region ap-southeast1 --model default --config '{"max_batch_size":64, "concurrency_limit":8}'
``` 

leo: applied. watching.

oncall-bot: ACTION: oncall handoff pending in 30m. Current oncall amanda.

julie: I'll prep a short notice for customers with affected SLA regions. nothing public yet, just targeted PMs.

nirav: proceeding with soft-quota now to shed 40% traffic from region to reduce pressure.

nirav: ```
# soft quota throttle
redwoodctl traffic quota set --region ap-southeast1 --policy soft --percent 60
``` 

nirav: set. traffic shaping engine reports 35% immediate drop. error rate dropping to ~7%.

amanda: good. but some legacy customers hit hard. leo, can we start a provider-reroute to provider-b for non-enterprise routes? strategy: move 50% of non-enterprise + 100% of canary traffic.

leo: executing provider reroute for non-enterprise.

leo: ```
redwoodctl traffic reroute --region ap-southeast1 --from provider-a --to provider-b --routes "default,canary" --weight 50
``` 

ops-bot: REROUTE_STARTED: 2165432142 by leo — checking target capacity.

ops-bot: REROUTE_PROGRESS: provider-b 25% -> 50% over 2m.

leo: reroute hit a rate limit on provider-b's capacity for long seq models, falling back some requests with 429. lowering weight to 30% and enabling model fallback to smaller variant.

leo: ```
redwoodctl traffic reroute --region ap-southeast1 --from provider-a --to provider-b --weight 30
redwoodctl model fallback --region ap-southeast1 --policy size-based --max_seq 512
``` 

amanda: also disabling optimizer-v2 feature flag in ap-southeast1. we've seen retries tied to it.

amanda: ```
redwoodctl feature toggle --region ap-southeast1 --feature optimizer-v2 --state off
``` 

julie: customer comms drafted. I'll send to Hana and product ops for approval: "We've detected elevated errors in APAC inference; temporary routing and quota changes applied; expected to improve within 30m."

sre-rotation: handing off to next oncall (nirav) — I'll stay in channel for 10m overlap. amanda, anything else?

amanda: thanks, leo/nirav. current status: errors down to 3-5%, latency trending down. provider-b load stabilized. leaving soft-quota in place for 20 more minutes then reevaluate. retention: collect a diffs of model latency pre/post.

nirav: will monitor for 45m, will start gradual rollback if stable. setting an alert for error >5% for 10m.

ops-bot: ALERT_CONFIGURED: watch error_rate_apac > 5% for 10m -> page oncall.

julie: sent targeted note to 8 high-impact customers (cc product-sla). no escalations yet.

leo: adding a postmortem ticket with initial notes and commands used.

amanda: closing loop — will reopen if any regression after rollback. great teamwork. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: resolved -> monitoring. closed at 2165433950.

amanda: thanks all, moving to post-incident review tasking (assigning followups in jira). :spiral_notepad:
